    Per-box agreement of free and wired random-cluster measures

    DefinitionWired-marginal difference between a box and its translate#✓fully proved

    StatMech.FK.fbd_offCentreCarrier

    The difference between the wired marginal of eb' on Λ_{N+k} and on the translate of Λ_{N+k} by v, evaluated at the translated edge.

    noncomputable def fbd_offCentreCarrier (N : ℕ) (v : Site d) (eb' : Sym2 (boxVerts d N))
    (p q : ℝ) (k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  edgeMargProb (wiredFkProb (boxGraph d (N + k)) (boxBoundary d (N + k)) p q)
      (innerEdgeLE d (Nat.le_add_right N k) eb')
    - edgeMargProb
        (wiredFkProb (fvs_transBoxGraph d (N + k) v) (fvs_transBoxBoundary d (N + k) v) p q)
        (Sym2.map (fvs_transEquiv d (N + k) v) (innerEdgeLE d (Nat.le_add_right N k) eb'))
    abbrev Site (d : ℕ) : Type := Fin d → ℤ

    noncomputable def fvs_transEquiv (d m : ℕ) (v : Site d) :
    boxVerts d m ≃ fvs_transBoxVerts d m v where
  toFun := fun x => ⟨(x : Site d) + v, by
    change ((x : Site d) + v - v) ∈ box d m
    rw [add_sub_cancel_right]; exact x.2⟩
  invFun := fun y => ⟨(y : Site d) - v, y.2⟩
  left_inv := by intro x; apply Subtype.ext; simp
  right_inv := by intro y; apply Subtype.ext; simp

    LemmaMonotone-coupled laws with equal edge marginals agree on up-sets#✓fully proved

    StatMech.FK.fk_unique_of_edgeMarg_eq

    Two monotonically coupled probability vectors with equal edge marginals agree on increasing events. Restatement of eventMass_eq_of_edgeMarg_eq (EdgeMarginal), kept because other modules use this name.

    lemma fk_unique_of_edgeMarg_eq {P : ConfigSpace E × ConfigSpace E → ℝ}
    {μ ν : ConfigSpace E → ℝ} (hP : IsMonotoneCouplingFun P μ ν)
    (hmarg : ∀ e : E, edgeMargProb μ e = edgeMargProb ν e)
    {A : Set (ConfigSpace E)} (hA : IsIncreasing A) :
    eventMassProb μ A = eventMassProb ν A
    abbrev ConfigSpace (E : Type*) : Type _ := E → Bool

    LemmaAgreement with a monotone map at continuity points fails countably#✓fully proved

    StatMech.FK.countable_edgeMarg_ne

    If a agrees with a monotone b at every continuity point of b, then {p | a p ≠ b p} is countable.

    lemma countable_edgeMarg_ne (hb : Monotone b)
    (heq_at_cont : ∀ p : ℝ, ContinuousAt b p → a p = b p) :
    {p : ℝ | a p ≠ b p}.Countable

    LemmaParametric agreement on increasing events off a countable set#✓fully proved

    StatMech.FK.phi0_eq_phi1_off_countable

    Parametric agreement: if for each p there is a monotone coupling of μ p and ν p, and edge marginals agree at every continuity point of the monotone map p ↦ ν_p(ω(e) = 1), then μ p and ν p agree on increasing events for all p outside a countable set.

    lemma phi0_eq_phi1_off_countable
    (μ ν : ℝ → ConfigSpace E → ℝ) (e : E)
    (P : ℝ → ConfigSpace E × ConfigSpace E → ℝ)
    (hcoup : ∀ p, IsMonotoneCouplingFun (P p) (μ p) (ν p))
    (hb : Monotone (fun p => edgeMargProb (ν p) e))
    (heq_at_cont : ∀ p : ℝ, ContinuousAt (fun p => edgeMargProb (ν p) e) p →
      ∀ e' : E, edgeMargProb (μ p) e' = edgeMargProb (ν p) e') :
    ∃ S : Set ℝ, S.Countable ∧
      ∀ p ∉ S, ∀ {A : Set (ConfigSpace E)}, IsIncreasing A →
        eventMassProb (μ p) A = eventMassProb (ν p) A
    abbrev ConfigSpace (E : Type*) : Type _ := E → Bool

    LemmaCountably many parameters admit a separating increasing event#✓fully proved

    StatMech.FK.countable_phi_ne

    Under the hypotheses of phi0_eq_phi1_off_countable, the set of p for which some increasing event separates μ p and ν p is countable.

    lemma countable_phi_ne
    (μ ν : ℝ → ConfigSpace E → ℝ) (e : E)
    (P : ℝ → ConfigSpace E × ConfigSpace E → ℝ)
    (hcoup : ∀ p, IsMonotoneCouplingFun (P p) (μ p) (ν p))
    (hb : Monotone (fun p => edgeMargProb (ν p) e))
    (heq_at_cont : ∀ p : ℝ, ContinuousAt (fun p => edgeMargProb (ν p) e) p →
      ∀ e' : E, edgeMargProb (μ p) e' = edgeMargProb (ν p) e') :
    {p : ℝ | ∃ A : Set (ConfigSpace E), IsIncreasing A ∧
        eventMassProb (μ p) A ≠ eventMassProb (ν p) A}.Countable
    abbrev ConfigSpace (E : Type*) : Type _ := E → Bool

    def rot_permBoxSym (d : ℕ) (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin d)) : BoxSym d where
  τ := rot_permEquiv d π
  adj := by
    intro x y
    simp only [hypercubicLattice_adj, rot_permEquiv_apply]
    rw [← Equiv.sum_comp π.symm (fun i => (x i - y i).natAbs)]
  box_mem := by
    intro n x
    simp only [mem_box, rot_permEquiv_apply]
    refine ⟨fun h i => ?_, fun h i => h (π.symm i)⟩
    have := h (π i); simpa using this
    structure BoxSym (d : ℕ) where
  /-- The underlying permutation of the sites. -/
  τ : Site d ≃ Site d
  /-- `τ` preserves nearest-neighbour adjacency. -/
  adj : ∀ x y, (hypercubicLattice d).Adj (τ x) (τ y) ↔ (hypercubicLattice d).Adj x y
  /-- `τ` maps each centered box onto itself. -/
  box_mem : ∀ n x, τ x ∈ box d n ↔ x ∈ box d n

    def rot_permEquiv (d : ℕ) (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin d)) : Site d ≃ Site d where
  toFun := fun x i => x (π.symm i)
  invFun := fun x i => x (π i)
  left_inv := by intro x; funext i; simp
  right_inv := by intro x; funext i; simp

    TheoremPer-box uniqueness of the random-cluster measures off a countable set#✓fully proved

    StatMech.FK.fkgq_countable_free_wired_disagreement

    For d ≥ 1, q ≥ 1, and every box Λ_N, the free and wired infinite-volume random-cluster measures on ℤ^d at p = logistic(t) give the same mass to every increasing event of Λ_N, for all t outside a countable set.

    This is a per-box statement only: the countable exceptional set may depend on N, the statement is in the logit parameter t rather than in p ∈ (0, 1) directly, and it concludes agreement on increasing events of that one finite restriction, not equality of the infinite-volume measures. No declaration here takes the countable union over N, transfers it to p, or derives equality of the infinite-volume measures. (Grimmett, The Random-Cluster Model, 2006, Theorem 4.60.)

    theorem fkgq_countable_free_wired_disagreement (hd : 1 ≤ d) (N : ℕ)
    (q : ℝ) (hq : 1 ≤ q) :
    {t : ℝ | ∃ A : Set (ConfigSpace (Sym2 (boxVerts d N))), IsIncreasing A ∧
      eventMassProb (fkgq_freeMass d N q hq t) A ≠
        eventMassProb (fkgq_wiredMass d N q hq t) A}.Countable
